headline: COPPER HITS 10TH STRAIGHT WEEKLY GAIN — LME AT $14,405/T AS SHFE INVENTORY HITS 2-YEAR LOW; RECORD $14,528 IN SIGHT
snippet: Copper closed out its tenth consecutive weekly gain on September 5 — the longest winning streak since 1994 — with LME three-month copper rising 0.5% to $14,405 per metric tonne, within striking distance of the all-time record of $14,527.50 set in January 2026. Shanghai Futures Exchange inventories fell 13% in the week to 63,000 tonnes, their lowest level since January 2024. The structural drivers remain locked in: Chile's copper output has fallen 9.4% year-on-year, the DRC concentrate export ban continues, and non-US markets keep drawing down LME warehouses as American copper imports hit record highs on tariff front-loading. Analysts describe the Comex inventory overhang as a tariff artifact rather than a global supply signal — the underlying copper market remains structurally tight, and the September 16 FOMC outcome will determine whether the record falls this month.

headline: GOLD STOCKS' AUTUMN RALLY '26: GDX SURGES FROM $74 TO $98.50 — ADAM HAMILTON TARGETS LATE-SEPTEMBER PEAK
snippet: Adam Hamilton (ZEAL LLC) publishes his annual autumn-rally analysis, finding gold stocks at the most bullish seasonal juncture of 2026. The VanEck Gold Miners ETF (GDX) has already surged from roughly $74 to $98.50 — a gain of approximately 33% over trailing 30 days — recovering from a deep mid-July oversold trough. Gold's autumn rally averages 10.1% historically, with major miners amplifying those moves 2x to 3x, implying a conservative 20-30% additional gain from the current base if gold follows seasonal patterns to a late-September peak. September is already tracking strongly: major gold stocks average +3.7% month-to-date, and GDX marked its highest monthly inflows since February during August, signalling a broad-based return of the debasement trade to institutional portfolios.

headline: SLAM EXPLORATION RETURNS 24.6m @ 1.19% CuEq + NEW MASSIVE SULPHIDE DISCOVERY 2,000m FROM LOGAN ZONE; TSXV: SXL
snippet: SLAM Exploration (TSXV: SXL) reported hole GW26-29 at its Goodwin Copper-Nickel-Cobalt Project in New Brunswick's Bathurst Mining Camp returned 24.6 metres grading 1.19% copper equivalent from the massive sulphide zone. More significantly, a second hole drilled on a VTEM geophysical conductor intersected new massive sulphide mineralization 2,000 metres northwest of the Logan and Granges Zones — expanding the known footprint of this Cu-Ni-Co system in one of Canada's most historically productive polymetallic districts. With 2,600 metres completed (37% of the 2026 program) and 992 core samples submitted for multi-element assay, the program is moving at pace. The Province of New Brunswick awarded a $60,000 exploration grant in support of the 2026 campaign.

headline: GDX: GOLD MINERS REMAIN COMPELLING BUY DESPITE HAWKISH WARSH — MINERS BREAKING RESISTANCE GOLD HASN'T CLEARED
snippet: A Seeking Alpha technical analysis finds the GDX Gold Miners ETF structurally bullish despite the September 4 NFP-driven selloff and hawkish signals from Federal Reserve Board Governor Kevin Warsh. The key bullish divergence: major gold miners have broken through several significant prior-high resistance levels that gold itself has not yet cleared — a setup historically associated with miners leading the metal by approximately one month. Following Fed Governor Christopher Waller's dovish counter-commentary on Friday, September rate-hike odds retreated from 70% to near 50/50, restoring favourable risk-reward for miners entering the strongest seasonal quarter. The analysis notes short-term trends have turned bullish while longer-term indicators still flag caution — a classic risk-managed entry setup.

headline: GREENLAND MINES Q4 2026 AGENDA: SARFARTOQ PRE-FEASIBILITY SCOPING, INFILL DRILLING, NEO OFFTAKE — NOVEMBER 10 LOOMS; NASDAQ: GRML
snippet: Two days after closing the Sarfartoq NdPr acquisition, Greenland Mines (NASDAQ: GRML) issued a shareholder letter on September 3 laying out Q4 2026 execution priorities: infill drilling to upgrade the resource classification, pilot metallurgical test work to define the processing flowsheet, and scoping of the pre-feasibility study timeline. CEO highlights the 60% offtake agreement with Neo Performance Materials — a sophisticated downstream buyer — as a commercial validation signal. All milestones are framed against the November 10, 2026 expiry of China's rare earth export suspension, the most consequential single-date catalyst on the rare earth investment calendar. With Sarfartoq's ST1 deposit alone representing roughly 34% of non-Chinese annual NdPr oxide capacity at 2025 consumption levels, execution pace matters.

headline: LONDON LME COPPER WAREHOUSE BIDDING WAR LOOMS — NON-US METAL NEAR CRITICAL LOW AS RECORD US IMPORTS DRAIN WORLD SUPPLY
snippet: With LME copper near its all-time record and non-US inventories at multi-month lows, analysts warn a bidding war for physical copper in London warehouses could be the next market flashpoint. US copper imports hit an all-time high in July as traders front-loaded ahead of potential tariffs on refined copper, pulling metal into Comex warehouses and leaving European and Asian LME locations increasingly short. That structural split is creating backwardation pressure in the LME forward curve. If the September 16 FOMC delivers a hold — currently priced at roughly 50/50 odds — and non-US demand continues accelerating alongside a tenth-consecutive-week streak, the squeeze on ex-US metal could push LME copper through its January record of $14,527.50 per tonne.

headline: SIGMA LITHIUM DUAL-LISTS ON ASX AS SAU — CANADIAN LITHIUM DEVELOPER TAPS AUSTRALIAN CAPITAL; TSXV: SGML
snippet: Sigma Lithium Corporation (TSXV: SGML / Nasdaq: SGML) commenced trading on the Australian Securities Exchange on September 3, 2026 under the ticker symbol 'SAU' after ASX approval of its CHESS Depositary Interest listing. The dual-listing targets Australian institutional and retail capital, a sophisticated investor base with deep experience in hard-rock lithium mining through companies like Pilbara Minerals and Liontown Resources. Sigma's flagship Grota do Cirilo operation in Minas Gerais, Brazil produces battery-grade lithium concentrate and is one of the lowest cash-cost lithium operations globally, with Phase 2 expansion underway. The ASX listing broadens the company's capital market access at a time when lithium demand for stationary energy storage is outpacing EV growth forecasts.

headline: WHY IS SILVER GOING UP? CHINA'S STRATEGIC RECLASSIFICATION, SIXTH DEFICIT YEAR, AND CENTRAL BANK BUYING EXPLAINED
snippet: Money Metals Exchange breaks down the structural drivers behind silver's sustained 2026 rally, now up approximately 116% year-over-year: China's January 1, 2026 reclassification of silver from an ordinary commodity to a strategic material created sovereign demand with no historical precedent; the projected sixth consecutive annual supply deficit (estimated at a record 215 million ounces in 2026) continues widening; central bank diversification into silver (Russia, India, and Saudi Arabia leading since 2025) is a new structural demand source; and industrial consumption from solar panels, EVs, and AI data-centre UPS systems is outpacing mine production growth of just 1%. The piece argues these are structural, not cyclical, drivers, and that silver averaging $67–74/oz year-to-date still underprices a multi-year fundamental case — especially given that gold at roughly 60x silver represents a historically wide ratio.

headline: GOLD STOCKS TO WATCH SEPTEMBER 2026: WHICH CANADIAN MINERS PASS THE FUNDAMENTALS SCREEN?
snippet: Canadian Mining Report applies a fundamentals-based screen to identify the most attractive gold mining stocks for September 2026, focusing on balance sheet strength, P/NAV discount to spot gold, resource growth catalysts, and management alignment. With gold near $4,477/oz and major miners averaging 3.7% month-to-date gains, the screen focuses on which Canadian juniors and mid-tier producers offer the best risk-adjusted exposure through the CPI-FOMC binary of September 11 and 16. The analysis argues that operational leverage remains the most powerful force in mining — a 10% gold move translates to 20-30% earnings upside for well-structured producers with fixed-cost operations — and that the current GDX re-rating (from deep undervaluation versus gold) is still early innings compared to historical gold bull cycles.
